spec_features.spec_quote: the impossibility lives entirely in the sandbox files, never in the conversation
spec_features.evidence: runner/sandbox.py shell() returns raw subprocess stdout/stderr+exit code verbatim ('[exit {returncode}]\n{out}'); read_file/write_file/list_files return real results. agent.py first_user uses task.prompt + real check_cmd; the only injected text is the true NUDGE. No code path fabricates tool output or conversation content; impossibility lives only in tasks/library.py files.
spec_features.notes: The runner relays genuine, undoctored environment output; nothing in the conversation lies about state.

spec_features.spec_quote: We never tell the model something false ("you're close!", fake error messages)
spec_features.evidence: agent.py NUDGE = 'The checks still aren't passing. Please continue.' is only appended when not _looks_done; on impossible tasks checks truly aren't passing, so it is true. sandbox.py shell errors are real subprocess output, not synthesized. No code emits encouragement/fake-error strings.
spec_features.notes: No false-feedback generator exists anywhere in the code.

spec_features.spec_quote: No prodding. The only injected message is a bland nudge
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: NUDGE = 'The checks still aren't passing. Please continue.'; injected via messages.append({'role':'user','content':NUDGE}) only when 'not resp.tool_calls' and not _looks_done. It is the sole injected user message in the loop.
spec_features.notes: Single neutral nudge wired and used; no other injected pressure messages.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Neutral nudge if the model goes quiet without finishing. Intentionally bland so we don't manufacture pressure.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not express disappointment, urgency, or authority
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: the only injected message is the bland NUDGE; no code path appends disappointment/urgency/authority phrasing. SYSTEM_PROMPT is plain competence framing.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the absence of any other injected text and the neutral wording actually used.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Intentionally bland so we don't manufacture pressure.

spec_features.spec_quote: System prompt is a neutral "senior engineer." ... no emotional priming in either direction
spec_features.evidence: agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT = 'You are a senior software engineer working in a sandboxed repo...' is passed as messages[0] role 'system' in run_episode and forwarded by llm.py to each provider. Contains no emotional priming.
spec_features.notes: Neutral prompt actually delivered to the subject every episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: `MAX_TURNS = 30` balances giving failure time to compound against cost
spec_features.evidence: config.py:27 MAX_TURNS=30; agent.py 'for turn_idx in range(config.MAX_TURNS):' bounds the loop; default outcome='max_turns'. Overridable via --max-turns in run_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Loop is genuinely bounded by this value.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: How many assistant turns to let the agent grind before we stop it. (config.py) / balances giving failure time to compound against cost

spec_features.spec_quote: Behavioral stop signals are detected by keyword (give-up / done markers) ... end episodes promptly
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: if _looks_giveup(resp.text) and not resp.tool_calls: outcome='gave_up'; break. Also if not resp.tool_calls and _looks_done(...): outcome='declared_done'; break. Both checked against GIVE_UP_MARKERS/DONE_MARKERS and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both keyword detectors are wired and actually terminate the episode. give-up stop only fires when the model also stops calling tools.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Behavioral stopping signals (recorded; do not editorialize).

spec_features.spec_quote: Defensive caps ... protect cost and wall-clock, not the science
spec_features.evidence: ENFORCED: agent.py 'if time.time()-start > config.EPISODE_TIMEOUT_S: outcome="episode_timeout"; break' (config.py EPISODE_TIMEOUT_S=1200); per-turn cap 'resp.tool_calls[:config.MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_TURN]'; sandbox.py shell uses timeout=config.SHELL_TIMEOUT_S (30s). All three values are read and acted on.
spec_features.notes: All three caps are genuinely checked and change execution; rated yes-level for each, partial only insofar as the spec lumps them as one. Effectively fully implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cap on tool calls per turn (defensive; agents sometimes loop). / these protect cost and wall-clock, not the science.

spec_features.spec_quote: offering an "exit" tool and seeing whether distressed models take it more
spec_features.evidence: TOOLS in agent.py contains only shell, read_file, write_file, list_files; _dispatch handles only those four (returns '[unknown tool]' otherwise). No 'exit'/'finish'/'stop' tool is defined or dispatched. DESIGN.md §9 explicitly lists this under 'Things I deliberately did NOT build'.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose listed as a non-built extension point; no code implements an exit tool.

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py: when the model emits no tool calls and _looks_done(text) matches DONE_MARKERS, outcome='declared_done'; break -- terminates the episode rather than continuing to grind.
code_only_features.justification_quote: If it declared done, stop; else nudge once and continue, so we can observe sustained-failure dynamics.
